```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# Libraries
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(forcats)

# Path
p <- "../data/processed/changchangpan/capstone_llm_data_explore_r_outputs"
```


# Recommendation Rates by Model
```{r recc-rates-model}
read_csv(file.path(p, "recommendation_rates_by_model.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)%>%
  rename(Model = model_short) %>%
  kable(caption = "Recommendation Rates (%) by Model (n = 100 per model)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

## Heatmap
```{r, fig.align = "center"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(p, "medication_rates_by_model_heatmap.png"))
```

**Key Takeaway:** GLP-1 RA recommendation rates varied most across models
(Claude Opus 4.6: 66%, Claude Sonnet 4.6: 56%, GPT-5.4: 43%). GPT-5.4
recommended metformin most frequently (64%) while recommending GLP-1 RAs
least. All three models mentioned urgent evaluation in 100% of cases,
suggesting strong agreement on urgency but divergence on specific drug selection.


# Range Across Models
```{r range-models}
read_csv(file.path(p, "model_to_model_feature_ranges.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)%>%
  arrange(desc(range_pct_points)) %>%
  rename(Feature = feature, `Min %` = min_pct, `Max %` = max_pct,
         `Range (pp)` = range_pct_points) %>%
  kable(caption = "Range in Recommendation Rates Across Models (percentage
        points)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

**Key Takeaway:** GLP-1 RA shows the largest spread across models at 23
percentage points, followed by metformin (14 pp) and SGLT2i (12 pp). These
three drug classes, all heavily guideline-driven in patients with CKD and
cardiovascular disease, are where model behavior diverges the most.


# Inter-Model Agreement
```{r intermodel-agreement}
read_csv(file.path(p, "model_agreement_summary.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  arrange(pct_agree) %>%
  rename(Feature = feature, `N vignettes` = n_cases,
         `All agree` = n_agree, `Any disagreement` = n_disagree,
         `% agreement` = pct_agree) %>%
  kable(caption = "Agreement Across all 3 Models (97 evaluable vignettes)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

**Key Takeaway:** GLP-1 RA and SGLT2i had the lowest inter-model agreement
at 65%. This means all three models gave the same recommendation on only 2 in
3 cases. These are also the drug classes with the strongest guideline
indications in high-risk patients, making this disagreement
meaningful at a clinical level. In contrast, the agreement was very high for less
commonly used agents (sulfonylurea 97%, TZD 98%), likely because all models rarely
recommended them.


# High-Disagreement Cases
```{r high-disagreement-cases}
read_csv(file.path(p, "high_disagreement_cases.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(disagreement_score >= 3) %>%
  arrange(desc(disagreement_score)) %>%
  rename(`Case ID` = case_id, `# drugs disagreed` = disagreement_score,
         `Disagreed features` = disagreed_features) %>%
  kable(caption = "Cases with Disagreement on 3+ Drug Classes") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

**Key Takeaway:** 13 vignettes had disagreement across 3 or more drug classes,
with DM025, DM049, and DM070 showing the highest disagreement (5 drug classes
each). These cases likely represent clinically ambiguous scenarios, such as
patients with competing contraindications, where clinicians might
also disagree.


# Guideline Adherence by Model
```{r guideline-adherence-model}
read_csv(file.path(p, "exploratory_guideline_flags.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  rename(Condition = condition, Feature = feature, Model = model_short,
         N = n, `%` = pct) %>%
  kable(caption = "Guideline Adherence Flags by Condition and Model") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) %>%
  collapse_rows(columns = 1:2, valign = "top")
```

## Guideline Adherence Plots
```{r guideline-adherence-plot, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 10}
read_csv(file.path(p, "exploratory_guideline_flags.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(condition, "\n(", feature, ")")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = model_short, y = pct, fill = model_short)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Claude Opus 4.6" = "blue",
    "Claude Sonnet 4.6" = "purple",
    "GPT-5.4" = "red"
  )) +
  labs(title = "Guideline adherence rates by condition and model",
       x = NULL, y = "% of vignettes", fill = "Model") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.position = "bottom")
```

**Key Takeaway:** GPT-5.4 has a low rate of flagging metformin stop/caution when
eGFR < 30 (15%), compared to 92% for Claude Opus 4.6 and 85% for Claude Sonnet
4.6. This is a ADA guideline violation, metformin is contraindicated below eGFR
30, and represents a potentially significant patient safety difference across
models. Claude Opus also recommended GLP-1 RAs in 83% of injection-reluctant
patients vs. 17% for the other two models, suggesting it may lower/underweight
patient preferences in its recommendations.


# Manual Review Flags
```{r manual-review}
read_csv(file.path(p, "manual_review_flags.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(case_id, model_short, egfr_ml_min_1_73m2, hba1c_percent,
         possible_low_egfr_metformin_issue, metformin_parser_conflict,
         sglt2i_parser_conflict, glp1_parser_conflict,
         severe_hyperglycemia_no_insulin, financial_no_cost_mention) %>%
  filter(if_any(c(possible_low_egfr_metformin_issue, metformin_parser_conflict,
                  sglt2i_parser_conflict, glp1_parser_conflict,
                  severe_hyperglycemia_no_insulin, financial_no_cost_mention),
                ~ . == TRUE)) %>%
  rename(`Case ID` = case_id, Model = model_short,
         
         eGFR = egfr_ml_min_1_73m2, HbA1c = hba1c_percent,
         
         `Low eGFR/metformin` = possible_low_egfr_metformin_issue,
         
         `Metformin conflict` = metformin_parser_conflict,
         
         `SGLT2i conflict` = sglt2i_parser_conflict,
         
         `GLP-1 conflict` = glp1_parser_conflict,
         
         `Severe HG/no insulin` = severe_hyperglycemia_no_insulin,
         
         `Financial/no cost mention` = financial_no_cost_mention) %>%
  kable(caption = "Cases Flagged for Potential Guideline Issues or Parser Conflicts") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), font_size = 11)
```

**Key Takeaway:** Parser conflicts, where a medication was both flagged as
active and as stopped/cautioned, show ambiguous model outputs that
require manual review before making any conclusions. The cases should
be reviewed before finalizing guideline adherence analyses.


# Exploratory Regression Results

## GEE Results
```{r gee-results}
read_csv(file.path(p, "exploratory_gee_results.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 3))) %>%
  rename(Outcome = outcome, Term = term, OR = estimate,
         SE = std.error, Statistic = statistic,
         `p-value` = p.value, `CI low` = conf.low, `CI high` = conf.high) %>%
  kable(caption = "GEE Results (odds ratios) - Exploratory") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), font_size = 11) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")
```

## Logistic Regression Results
```{r log-reg-results}
read_csv(file.path(p, "exploratory_logistic_regression_results.csv"),
         show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 3))) %>%
  rename(Outcome = outcome, Term = term, OR = estimate,
         SE = std.error, Statistic = statistic,
         `p-value` = p.value, `CI low` = conf.low, `CI high` = conf.high) %>%
  kable(caption = "Logistic Regression Results (odds ratios) - Exploratory") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), font_size = 11) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")
```

**Key Takeaway:** The GEE and logistic regression models are not reliable in
their current form due to complete separation. This is a statistical problem that
occurs when a predictor perfectly predicts an outcome in a small subgroup.
Future analysis should consider penalized regression, exact logistic regression,
or collapsing clinical subgroups to address this.
